candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the $close leaf: $close is adjusted while $low/$high are raw, so the ratio silently mixes two price scales. Swapped $close to $open (raw), preserving the stochastic-range structure; all fields are now raw and scale-consistent.
Same scale bug as its sibling factor: TS_MAX($high,21) (raw) minus $close (adjusted). Swapped $close to $open to restore scale consistency with $high; the liquidity normalizer is untouched.

Weakest component is the RANK operator: every other surviving factor standardizes cross-sectionally with CS_RANK, this one uses plain RANK, risking a non-cross-sectional or lookahead-prone ranking. Single-node swap to CS_RANK; not a crossover, so working-memory rule 1 does not apply.

Weakest point is stability (3 negative years): a flat 21-day mean lags regime shifts. Per rule 5, varied functional form instead of window: TS_MEAN to EMA, same window and fields, so correlation with the dollar-volume archive neighbor (0.779) should fall rather than breach the gate.

Weakest link is the 3.0-day IC half-life paired with 0.273 turnover: the ratio decays faster than it can be traded profitably. Added a 5-day smoothing wrapper around the whole ratio to extend persistence and cut whipsaw, leaving fields and the 15-day window untouched to avoid rule 5's correlation-gate trap.

Weakest component is the TS_MEAN level statistic: per rule 6, a dollar-volume level or mean proposed alone is already saturated against the archive. Swapped to TS_DELTA to capture liquidity trend instead of level (a genuine reordering, not a monotonic transform) and added CS_RANK, since this was the only parent with no cross-sectional standardization at all.

Weakest point is turnover (0.516, the largest cost drag in the set), driven by single-day volume noise inside the rank term. Smoothed the numerator with a 3-day mean; the SIGN reversal trigger and its 2-day window are untouched, so this targets noise, not the reversal logic that also coincides with the 2010-2013 regime flip.

Highest turnover in the whole set (0.598) despite a half-life over 63 days: daily churn from the unsmoothed single-day range numerator is not earned back by any fast-decaying signal. Smoothed the numerator over 3 days to match its true slow horizon; denominator and window untouched.

Worst stability in the set (0.57, negative in 2001 and 2009, both well-known momentum-crash years). Standard fix for raw 126-day momentum: skip the most recent month before summing so the ranking signal stops overlapping with short-term reversal. Denominator vol estimate is left as-is.

Weakest factor in the round (t 1.25, ICIR 0.020); the fastest leg, a flat 5-day volume mean, is the noisiest input feeding the spread. Per rule 5, swapped it to EMA (functional-form change, not a window change) to weight recent days more and reduce noise in the fast term.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Crossover proposals multiplying or adding the ROA rank with an unrelated price-based rank term keep failing the fusion check for sharing only 2 nodes; avoid shallow top-level fusions with ROA this round.
  2. Rank or argmax transforms applied directly to raw volume or dollar volume, with no normalization, failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.46 to 0.74); use volume/dollar volume as a normalizer inside a feature, not as the ranked quantity itself.
  3. Correlating volume (or sign of return) with returns over 21 to 63 day windows produced the weakest scores of the round (|t| 0.02 to 0.36); deprioritize volume-return correlation as a feature family.
  4. A 252-day window on volume or dollar volume dropped coverage to exactly 0.874 in both instances this round, just under the 0.90 floor, while 63-day windows on the same fields passed coverage fine; avoid 252-day volume windows.
  5. Changing only the lookback window on an already-archived expression (10 vs 21, or 63 vs 21) reliably triggers the correlation gate at rho 0.94 to 0.98; vary the functional form, not just window length, when building on archived structures.
  6. Raw dollar volume and its medium-window mean both duplicate the archived short-window dollar-volume mean at rho above 0.93; this normalizer is saturated, so pair dollar volume with a new signal rather than proposing it alone.
  7. All three accepts this round pair a price range (high-low or high-close distance) with a dollar-volume or liquidity-rank normalizer, spanning fast, medium, and slow speed niches; this structure is currently the productive one, favor it over fundamentals crossovers.
  8. A near-duplicate of the round's top accepted factor, differing by one normalizer swap, was rejected for sharing 5 nodes with it; edits to a freshly-accepted winner need a different normalizer or range definition, not a single-node swap, to count as novel.
